headlines.article_text: Tech stocks sell-off: SK Hynix, Samsung, SoftBank Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Asian technology stocks tumbled Friday, tracking a sharp sell-off on Wall Street overnight that sent the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite into correction territory. Images of mobile devices at the Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) Museum of Innovation in Hsinchu, on Tuesday, Jan. 11, 2022. I-Hwa Cheng | Bloomberg | Getty Images Asian technology stocks tumbled Friday, tracking a sharp sell-off on Wall Street overnight that sent the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite into correction territory as renewed concerns over artificial intelligence spending rattled investor sentiment. South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix plunged 10.44%, while Samsung Electronics shed 6.35%. LG Innotek and LG Display fell 7.02% and 4.45%, respectively, as selling pressure spread across the country's technology sector. The rout came as investors worried that Democrats' sweeping victory in the U.S. midterm elections could lead to tighter restrictions on data-center development, potentially slowing demand for AI chips and related infrastructure. I n Japan, semiconductor-related stocks also fell, with chip-testing equipment maker Advantest plunging 4.99%, while Tokyo Electron slid over 5%. Technology investment giant SoftBank Group tumbled 10.83%. Shares of memory chipmaker Kioxia Holdings fell 8.72%, while Renesas Electronics declined 5.74%. watch now VIDEO 5:46 05:46 Hyperscalers, healthcare and financials are opportunities in this big sell-off Squawk Box Asia In Taiwan, semiconductor stocks also came under heavy selling pressure, with contract chipmaker TSMC sliding 4.69%. China was also caught in the regional sell-off, with the tech-heavy STAR Market and the ChiNext Artificial Intelligence Index both tumbling more than 4%. The declines followed a brutal session on Wall Street, where the Nasdaq Composite sank 5.5%, amid mounting concerns over the sustainability of the AI investment boom and returns on massive data-center spending. It closed more than 10% below its recent peak. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plunged 12.2%. European stocks were broadly lower on Friday, but technology was among the least-impacted sectors, with losses of around 0.25% in morning deals. Chip stocks ASML and ASMI rose 4% and 3%, respectively. The sell-off in Asian equities has been exacerbated by investors unwinding positions, stop-loss selling and heightened volatility, Timothy Moe, chief Asia Pacific equity strategist at Goldman Sachs, told CNBC's "Squawk Box Asia" on Friday. He added that potential political opposition to U.S. data center construction may affect demand and profits for Asian AI hardware suppliers. "If there's concern about the speed and magnitude of buildout in the U.S., then obviously that's going to put all that into question," he said. "The market's tendency is always to shoot first and ask questions later. I think that's exactly what's happening now."
